refs: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 91, nutrition and leak

steps.say: ERAS pathways with carbohydrate loading two hours preoperatively, no bowel prep for colonic cases, avoiding thoracic epidural in laparoscopy and day one mobilisation cut stay by two to three days. Every element is small, but together they transform recovery. Audit compliance, since missed elements erase the benefit.
steps.tx: **ERAS** pathways with **carbohydrate loading** **2** hours preoperatively, no bowel prep for colonic cases, thoracic epidural avoidance in laparoscopy and day-**1** mobilisation cut stay by **2** to **3** days. Chewing gum, early catheter removal and opioid-sparing analgesia complete the bundle, and compliance over 70 percent predicts the full benefit. Laparoscopy plus ERAS beats either alone for length of stay.

steps.say: Prehabilitation with four weeks of exercise, protein one point five grams per kilo and anaemia correction with intravenous iron reduces complications in frail GI surgery patients. Frailty is modifiable in the waiting window. Use neoadjuvant time to train, not just to wait.
steps.tx: **Prehabilitation** with **4** weeks of exercise, **protein target** **1.5** g per kg and anaemia correction with intravenous iron reduces complications in frail GI surgery patients. Inspiratory muscle training, walking programmes and immunonutrition stack with iron repletion, and cardiopulmonary testing tracks fitness gains. Delaying cancer surgery briefly to prehabilitate pays back in fewer leaks and chest infections.

steps.say: Feeding jejunostomy placed distal to oesophageal, gastric and pancreatic anastomoses starts trickle feeds at twenty four hours. Tube blockage and diarrhoea are the commonest issues. Flush protocols and fibre-free starter feeds prevent most interruptions.
steps.tx: **Feeding jejunostomy** placed distal to oesophageal, gastric and pancreatic anastomoses starts **trickle feeds** at **24** hours, with tube blockage and diarrhoea as commonest issues. Fine-bore flushing with water before and after drugs keeps the tube patent, and slow rate escalation with low-fat formula settles diarrhoea. Nasojejunal tubes bridge short needs, reserving surgical jejunostomy for prolonged recovery.

steps.say: Anastomotic leak grades from radiologic only through to peritonitis needing reoperation. CRP over one fifty on day three to five triggers CT with rectal contrast. Never watch rising CRP after colorectal anastomosis.
steps.tx: **Anastomotic leak** grades A radiologic through C with peritonitis needing reoperation, with **C-reactive protein** over **150** mg per L on day **3** to **5** triggering CT with rectal contrast. Tachycardia with ileus out of proportion to the operation day warns earlier than fever, and drain fluid amylase or bilirubin confirms the leak. Diverting stomas reduce symptomatic leak and emergency reoperation after low rectal anastomosis, and they convert catastrophes into manageable fistulae.

steps.say: Endoscopic vacuum sponge therapy every three days closes contained rectal leaks with eighty percent success. Early defects under two weeks suit transanal suture repair instead. Choose by defect age and cavity size.
steps.tx: Endoscopic **vacuum sponge** therapy every **3** days closes contained rectal leaks with **80** percent success, while early defects under **2** weeks suit **transanal repair**. Sponge exchanges debride and granulate the presacral cavity from inside, and **transanal suture** closes fresh small defects before fibrosis sets in. Large chronic cavities with strictures need redo anastomosis or permanent diversion instead.

steps.say: High output enterocutaneous fistula over five hundred millilitres a day with sepsis gets Sepsis Nutrition Anatomy Procedure care. Definitive surgery waits at least three months, usually three to six, until FRIENDS factors resolve. Operating into hostile inflammation guarantees another fistula.
steps.tx: High-output **enterocutaneous fistula** over **500** mL per day with sepsis gets Sepsis-Nutrition-Anatomy-Procedure care, with definitive surgery no earlier than **3** months and usually **3** to **6** months when **FRIENDS** factors resolve. Distal obstruction, steroids and sepsis each forbid early repair, and octreotide with parenteral nutrition buys time. Definitive take-down with single anastomosis follows only when albumin, weight and sepsis all normalise.

steps.say: Refeeding syndrome with phosphate under zero point six after five days starvation needs thiamine before feeds with slow calorie build over four to seven days. Feeding a starved heart too fast arrests it. Check phosphate, magnesium and potassium before every increase.
steps.tx: **Refeeding syndrome** with phosphate under **0.6** mmol per L after **5** days starvation needs **thiamine** before feeds with slow calorie build over **4** to **7** days. Insulin surge drives phosphate, potassium and magnesium intracellularly, collapsing cardiac and respiratory muscle. Start at 10 kcal per kg with full vitamin cover, and replace electrolytes aggressively before each step up.

steps.say: Sarcopenia with psoas index below cutoffs doubles leak and mortality. Screen by CT morphomics with five to seven days of immunonutrition with arginine before major HPB resection. Muscle mass predicts surgical risk better than weight.
steps.tx: **Sarcopenia** with psoas index below cutoffs doubles leak and mortality, screened by CT morphomics with **5 to 7** days of **immunonutrition** with arginine before major HPB resection. Low muscle plus myosteatosis marks the frail phenotype even in obesity, and prehabilitation exercise stacks with arginine-enhanced feeds. Document the psoas index in every HPB multidisciplinary meeting as a formal risk variable.
